title: Methods of sterilization
definition: Complete destruction of all microbes including spores.
keyPoints: Physical: autoclave (121°C, 15 psi, 15-20 min — steam under pressure; commonest hospital method), dry heat (hot air oven 160°C/2 h), boiling (disinfection only), radiation (gamma for single-use), filtration (HEPA 0.22 μm)
Chemical: ethylene oxide (heat-sensitive), glutaraldehyde (high-level disinfection), hydrogen peroxide plasma
clinicalContext: Nurse prepares instruments for OT use.
nursingPriority: Load autoclave correctly (loosely packed, indicators), confirm 121°C/15 psi/15-20 min, check chemical and biological indicators (Bacillus stearothermophilus), document cycle.

title: Viral families classification
keyPoints: DNA: Herpes, Pox, Adeno, Papilloma, Parvo, Hepadna (HBV)
RNA: Picorna (polio, hep A), Retro (HIV), Orthomyxo (flu), Paramyxo (measles, mumps), Rhabdo (rabies), Flavi (dengue, yellow fever, hep C), Filo (Ebola), Corona, Toga (rubella)
Enveloped vs non-enveloped (enveloped more susceptible to disinfection)
nursingPriority: Examples: HIV, influenza, measles, RSV, rabies, hepatitis C, corona.

title: Hepatitis viruses (A-E)
keyPoints: A (HAV): RNA picornavirus, fecal-oral, self-limited, vaccine
B (HBV): DNA hepadna, blood/sex/vertical, chronic risk, vaccine (birth + 6/10/14 wk)
C (HCV): RNA flavi, blood, chronic, DAAs curative
E (HEV): RNA hepe, fecal-oral, pregnancy high mortality
clinicalContext: Pregnant woman with acute hepatitis and jaundice.
nursingPriority: Suspect hepatitis E (high fetal/maternal mortality); supportive care, monitor PT/INR, isolate, deliver per obstetric plan.

title: Epstein-Barr virus
keyPoints: Symptoms: fever, exudative pharyngitis, lymphadenopathy, splenomegaly, atypical lymphocytes
Complications: splenic rupture (avoid contact sports 4 wk), Burkitt lymphoma, nasopharyngeal ca
clinicalContext: Teen with sore throat, fever, huge cervical nodes, splenomegaly, monospot positive.
nursingPriority: Supportive — rest, hydration, analgesia (avoid ampicillin — rash), avoid contact sports 3-4 wk, ENT review.

title: Mumps
clinicalContext: Teen with bilateral parotid swelling and fever.
nursingPriority: Isolate droplet precautions 5 d post-swelling, analgesia, cold/warm compress, hydration, observe for complications (orchitis, meningitis).

title: HIV — virus structure
keyPoints: Core: p24 capsid, RNA, reverse transcriptase, integrase, protease
nursingPriority: p24 antigen (detectable earliest with RNA PCR), confirm with ELISA/Western blot; initiate ART per NACO guideline.

title: HPV
nursingPriority: HPV vaccine 2-dose schedule 0 and 6 mo (<15 y), educate about cervical cancer prevention.

title: Rotavirus
definition: Major cause of pediatric severe diarrhea.
keyPoints: Vaccine: oral rota vaccine (6, 10, 14 wk) in UIP
Prevention: hand hygiene, safe water, exclusive BF
clinicalContext: 8-mo-old with severe watery diarrhea and dehydration.
nursingPriority: Assess dehydration, ORS/IV per Plan A/B/C, zinc, continue breastfeeding, ensure vaccine up to date, droplet precautions.

title: Motility tests
keyPoints: Flagella specific: polar (Pseudomonas), lophotrichous, peritrichous (E coli)
nursingPriority: Cite hanging drop or semisolid agar.

title: Acid-fast stain (Ziehl-Neelsen)
keyPoints: Carbol fuchsin + heat, decolorize with acid-alcohol, counterstain methylene blue
Acid-fast bacilli (AFB) appear red on blue background
nursingPriority: 3 early morning samples, ZN stain, culture if positive, GeneXpert for rapid MTB/rifampicin resistance.

title: Tyndallization
keyPoints: Allows spores to germinate then kills them
Used for heat-labile materials (e.g. media with sugar)
nursingPriority: Recall as Tyndallization.

title: Rod-shaped bacteria
keyPoints: Gram+: Bacillus, Clostridium, Listeria, Corynebacterium, Mycobacterium (acid-fast)
Gram-: E coli, Klebsiella, Salmonella, Shigella, Proteus, Pseudomonas, Vibrio (curved), Helicobacter (spiral)
nursingPriority: Bacillus, Clostridium, Listeria, Corynebacterium.

title: Gram-positive organisms
nursingPriority: Staphylococcus in clusters; Streptococcus in chains.

title: Heterotrophs vs autotrophs
keyPoints: Autotrophs: CO2 as C source (photo- or chemo-)
Heterotrophs: organic compounds as C source
nursingPriority: Recognize heterotroph usage.

title: Endotoxin vs exotoxin
keyPoints: Endotoxin: LPS cell wall of Gram-, heat stable, low potency, non-specific (fever, shock), no vaccine
Exotoxin: secreted protein, heat labile, high potency, specific effect (tetanus, diphtheria, botulinum), toxoid vaccines
nursingPriority: Cite endotoxin (Gram-negative lipopolysaccharide).

title: Bacterial growth curve
nursingPriority: Most antibiotics most effective on log phase.

title: Neisseria gonorrhoeae
keyPoints: Cervicitis, urethritis, PID, septic arthritis, ophthalmia neonatorum
Treatment: ceftriaxone 500 mg IM + azithromycin (or doxycycline)
Prevent ophthalmia: erythromycin 0.5% eye ointment at birth
nursingPriority: Single IM ceftriaxone 500 mg + oral azithromycin 1 g stat, partner notification, test for other STIs (syphilis, HIV).

title: Salmonella typhi (typhoid)
keyPoints: Features: step-ladder fever, relative bradycardia, rose spots, hepatosplenomegaly, constipation then diarrhea
Diagnosis: blood culture (1st wk), stool/urine (2nd-3rd wk), Widal (less specific)
clinicalContext: 15-y-old with 10 d of fever, relative bradycardia, rose spots.
nursingPriority: Blood culture x2 before antibiotic, start IV ceftriaxone 2 g OD, maintain hydration, monitor for complications (perforation, hemorrhage).

title: Borrelia
keyPoints: B burgdorferi: Lyme disease (erythema migrans, arthritis, neuro, cardio)
clinicalContext: Hiker with expanding bulls-eye rash and fever.
nursingPriority: Erythema migrans of Lyme — doxycycline 100 mg BD x14-21 d (<8 y amox), educate tick removal.

title: Treponema pallidum (syphilis)
keyPoints: Secondary: maculopapular rash including palms/soles, condyloma lata (6 wk-6 mo)
nursingPriority: Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million U IM stat (early), 3 doses 1 wk apart (late/unknown); desensitize if allergy; partner treat; HIV screen.

title: Vibrio cholerae
definition: Comma-shaped Gram-negative, cholera toxin causing rice-water stool.
keyPoints: Treatment: aggressive rehydration (ORS Plan A/B/C or IV RL), doxycycline shortens illness
Vaccine: Shanchol oral killed for outbreak
nursingPriority: Isolate, aggressive IV Ringer Lactate, ORS, doxycycline 300 mg single dose adult, chlorination of water, notify public health.

title: Food poisoning — bacterial
keyPoints: Preformed toxin (1-6 h): S aureus, B cereus emetic
Onset 8-16 h: C perfringens, B cereus diarrheal
Onset 12-72 h: Salmonella, Shigella, E coli, Campylobacter
Botulism (12-36 h): flaccid paralysis from C botulinum
clinicalContext: Family develops vomiting 3 h after mayonnaise salad.
nursingPriority: Suspect Staph aureus preformed toxin — supportive, hydration, antiemetic, no antibiotic usually needed.

title: Streptococcus
keyPoints: Beta-hemolytic: Group A (pyogenes, rheumatic fever, PSGN, scarlet fever, pharyngitis, impetigo)
Group B (agalactiae, neonatal sepsis, screen in pregnancy)
nursingPriority: Oral amoxicillin 50 mg/kg/d x10 d to prevent rheumatic fever, analgesia, hydration.

title: Clostridium perfringens (gas gangrene)
keyPoints: Wound with dirt, crepitus, rapid progression, hemolysis
Treatment: surgical debridement, IV penicillin + clindamycin, HBO2 adjunct
clinicalContext: Trauma patient with crepitus and rapid necrosis around wound.
nursingPriority: Emergent surgical debridement, IV penicillin G 4 MU q4 h + clindamycin, HBO2 if available, supportive care.

title: Clostridium tetani
keyPoints: Classical: trismus, risus sardonicus, opisthotonus, autonomic instability
Treatment: HTIG, metronidazole, wound debridement, benzo for spasm
clinicalContext: Farmer with deep puncture wound, unvaccinated 10 y.
nursingPriority: Clean debride, HTIG 250 U IM + Td vaccine, metronidazole 500 mg IV, tetanus prevention education.

title: Escherichia coli
definition: Gram- rod; commensal and pathogenic strains.
clinicalContext: Child with bloody diarrhea, hemolytic anemia, thrombocytopenia, renal failure.
nursingPriority: Suspect EHEC HUS — supportive (no antibiotic; risk of toxin release), hydrate, dialysis if needed, do not give anti-motility agents.

title: Mycoplasma
definition: Smallest free-living bacteria; no cell wall.
keyPoints: M pneumoniae: atypical pneumonia, walking pneumonia, bullous myringitis, cold agglutinins
Beta-lactams ineffective — use macrolide, doxycycline, fluoroquinolone
clinicalContext: College student with dry cough, fever, bullous myringitis.
nursingPriority: Azithromycin 500 mg day 1 then 250 mg x4 d or doxycycline 100 mg BD; educate about prolonged cough.

title: Entamoeba histolytica
definition: Protozoa causing amoebic dysentery and liver abscess.
keyPoints: Liver abscess: anchovy-sauce pus in right lobe
clinicalContext: Traveler with right upper quadrant pain and liver abscess.
nursingPriority: Metronidazole 750 mg TDS x10 d + luminal agent, drainage only if imminent rupture, avoid alcohol.

topic: Schick, Lepromin, Frei, Dick, Widal tests
title: Schick, Lepromin, Frei, Dick, Widal tests
nursingPriority: Memorize the table.

title: Aspergillus
clinicalContext: Neutropenic post-transplant with fever and lung infiltrate with halo sign.
nursingPriority: Voriconazole IV (or isavuconazole), serum galactomannan, HEPA-filtered room, reverse neutropenia.

title: Immunity — definition
keyPoints: Innate: present at birth (skin, mucus, complement, NK)
Adaptive: acquired, specific (B and T cells, antibodies)
nursingPriority: Distinguish non-specific innate from specific adaptive.

title: Active immunity
nursingPriority: Natural active immunity — long-lasting, book UIP record.

title: Passive immunity
keyPoints: Natural passive: transplacental IgG, breast milk IgA
Artificial passive: immunoglobulin (HBIg, VZIg, rabies IG, anti-tetanus)
nursingPriority: HBIg within 12 h of birth + Hep B vaccine birth dose, complete Hep B schedule.

title: Herd immunity
definition: Indirect protection when vaccination coverage is high.
clinicalContext: Measles outbreak in community with 80% coverage.
nursingPriority: Campaign to achieve >=95%, targeted catch-up immunization, trace index cases, isolate, vitamin A.

title: Innate immunity
nursingPriority: Cite skin and mucosal barriers.

title: Artificial immunity
nursingPriority: Equine/human anti-rabies immunoglobulin (passive) + rabies vaccine (active) — Essen schedule.

title: Hypersensitivity reactions (I-IV)
keyPoints: Type I: IgE immediate (anaphylaxis, atopy, allergic asthma)
Type II: antibody-mediated cytotoxic (hemolytic anemia, Goodpasture)
Type III: immune complex (SLE, PSGN, serum sickness)
Type IV: delayed cell-mediated (contact dermatitis, TB Mantoux)
clinicalContext: Mantoux reading at 48 h with 15 mm induration.
nursingPriority: Type IV delayed hypersensitivity — interpret per immune status (>=10 mm positive for most).

title: Immunoglobulin classes (IgA-IgM)
keyPoints: IgA: secretions, mucosal (saliva, tears, breast milk)
nursingPriority: Secretory IgA in breast milk (colostrum esp rich).

title: Cell-mediated immunity
keyPoints: CD4 helper T cells: coordinate via cytokines
CD8 cytotoxic T: kill infected/cancer cells
clinicalContext: HIV patient susceptible to TB and Pneumocystis.
nursingPriority: Cell-mediated immunity impaired — prophylaxis (isoniazid, cotrimoxazole), ART initiation, monitor CD4.
